thread:
maria: Heads up — spotted a latency spike on MI250 for seq_len=128 workloads this morning. p95 went from ~45ms to ~120ms for a subset of requests. Suspect we’re missing a specialized GEMM kernel so runtime falls back to the generic path.

aj: Can you paste the minimal repro and profiler snapshot?

maria: Repro command: `./run_inference -m redwood-bloom-7b -s 128 -b 1 --device mi250`

Profiler snippet (perf-bot attached):
```
TIMESTAMP: 2024-11-20T09:12:10Z
kernel_lookup: missing (mi250, op=matmul, dtype=fp16, seqlen=128)
fallback_path: cu_generic_matmul
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.62
avg_token_latency: 118.4ms
```

ryan: Oof. That lookup line implies our kernel inventory for mi250 has a gap at seqlen=128 for that op/dtype combo. Could be a packaging omission or autotuner skipped it.

aj: I checked the packaging manifest — the binary list contains mi250 kernels for seqlen 64 and 256 but not 128 (`kernels.mi250.manifest` excerpt).

jamie: Is this amplified by batching heuristics? We may be coalescing into an inefficient tiling choice when batch size is low.

maria: For these hits batch=1 but we do combine dynamic batching in the serving layer. The spike reproduces without batching too.

perf-bot: Quick perf diffs from nightly CI (yesterday vs last week):
- model: redwood-bloom-7b
- hardware: mi250
- metric: p95 token latency
- before: 46.1ms
- after: 112.7ms
- change: +144%

ryan: Two-pronged plan: 1) short term routing change to prefer a compatible smaller-seqlen kernel (soft route) before falling to generic; 2) longer term ensure autotuner populates the 128 kernel or our packaging includes a polyfilled kernel.

aj: For (1) we can add a conditional route rule in runtime config:
```
route_policy {
  when kernel_missing && hw == "mi250" && op == "matmul" {
    prefer_kernel(seqlen=64, allow_polyfill=true, max_extra_latency_ms=30)
  }
}
```
This will pick a close match that keeps latency under SLO in many cases.

jamie: Need to be careful — polyfill kernels can blow memory/kv-cache behavior. If we pick a different tiling, KV cache alignment might change and increase KV eviction thrash. Any KV metrics?

maria: KV cache evictions ticked up by ~8% in the same window. Logs show more frequent full-cache writes after fallback events.

ryan: Ok add a gating check: only apply soft-route if kv_eviction_rate_change < 0.1 (10%). That avoids making tail-case worse.

aj: I'll push a hotfix branch that implements the soft-route and the gating. Patch will include telemetry flags so we can flip it remote.

perf-bot: CI warm-run of soft-route patch (simulated): p95 reduced to 58.9ms, kv_eviction_delta reported +0.02. Looks promising.

maria: Nice. For the long term I’ll open an autotune job to force submission of candidate kernels for seqlen 128 on mi250. If autotuner still rejects it, we may need manual kernel generation or a quantized path.

jamie: Also add an eval set that exercises KV edgecases (long context + short prompts) so we can detect regressions earlier.

aj: Deploying hotfix to a canary (10% of traffic) now. Will notify SLO channels.

sre-oncall: pinged oncall, will watch error/latency alerts and rollback if >5% error rate or p99 > 300ms for 5m.

maria: Thanks. Follow-ups: (A) aj: PR and canary link; (B) maria: autotune job + ticket; (C) jamie: KV-focused eval set.

ryan: If the manual kernel ends up needed, call in platform infra for build support — MI250 cross-compilation can be fiddly.

maria: Will update thread with PR link and perf snapshots once canary has 2 hours of traffic. :hourglass:
